PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.

items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(c) covers fittings needed for the failed heating-pipe section. The four-piece gross benchmark is €42, subject to verification that all four were needed.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) exclude duplicated or unsupported fittings. The second four-piece set is not substantiated by the localized repair description; if separately verified, the benchmark is €42.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary like-for-like fittings, but §7.1.8(e) requires evidence that the five 28 mm elbows were used on the affected section. The five-piece benchmark is €104.
Under §7.1.8(e), the additional five elbows must be attributable to the documented joint repair, which does not establish that quantity. If verified, the five-piece benchmark is €103.
A single transition fitting is plausible under §7.1.7(c), although its use on the affected section still needs confirmation under §7.1.8(e). The one-piece benchmark is €21.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary fasteners for the pipe repair. The eight-piece gross benchmark is €9.30.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary pipe supports, but §7.1.8(e) requires the size and quantity to match the repair. The four-piece benchmark is €19.20.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers clamps needed to secure the repaired pipe. Four clamps at about €5.25 gross each give €21, provided they are distinct from the other clamp line.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour, and this block is consistent with the reported site time. The 6.75-hour gross benchmark is €619.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper labour, and the description confirms a helper attended for part of the job. The 5.75-hour gross benchmark is €409.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(e) limit this to pipe attributable to the repair; about one metre was replaced, so the billed 6.4 m is not supported on the current record. If the full quantity is substantiated, the gross benchmark is €99.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows one travel charge per contractor per invoice for the repair. The gross benchmark for this first charge is €80.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers installation consumables actually used, provided they do not duplicate itemized parts under §7.1.8(c). The gross benchmark is €43.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes contractor processing charges added to itemized labour and materials. The €15 figure is a nominal conditional estimate only.

Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like insulation, but §7.1.8(e) requires the billed six metres to match the work; only local re-insulation is described. If all six metres are substantiated, the gross benchmark is €135.
Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) exclude duplicate or unsupported insulation, and no separate use for six mats is described. If verified as distinct and necessary, six mats at about €15 gross give €90.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers wire used to secure the reinstated insulation. The two-piece gross benchmark is €26, subject to the quantity matching the repair.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers the second labour block if it records distinct repair time; the combined 13.75 technician hours broadly fit the reported attendance. The seven-hour gross benchmark is €642.
Section 7.1.7(f) limits travel to the first charge for this contractor on this invoice, even if the same repair required a return visit. The conditional benchmark for a covered trip would be €80.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes contractor protective equipment, and the bundled set does not separately identify any covered repair consumables. A basic set would cost about €20 gross if payable.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of the removed pipe and insulation, without double recovery. The small-job gross benchmark is €60.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a) may allow necessary cleanup of leak residues on the affected tiles, but the bundled coating is not documented as reinstatement of a damaged pre-loss finish. If the necessary local cleanup can be separated, allow about €100 gross, not the full five hours.
